subject: Consolidated access artifacts for SIG intake — delivery plan
messages:
From: Elena Ortiz <elena@alphamed.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: SIG intake — initial list of access artifacts we need

Marissa,

Thanks for making time to support AlphaMed's SIG intake. To keep the review tight, our compliance team asked for a consolidated package covering authentication, provisioning, and authorization controls. Can you confirm you can provide the following items? Ideally as a single ZIP with a short index file that maps files to SIG questions.

- SCIM delta export (last 30 days) + full snapshot for entitlements; include schema version and sample user objects.
- SAML assertion samples for two active users (one admin, one standard user) showing typical attributes and timestamps.
- RBAC matrix (roles -> permissions) and a brief least-privilege rationale for service accounts.
- Evidence of provision/deprovision workflow (owner contact, ticket IDs, and any automation runbooks).
- Session/session lifetime settings and MFA enrollment stats for admin population.

If you can share a canary subset first (anonymized sample of 10 users) for quick verification, that helps speed the review. We may redact PII on our side but please label any files that contain real emails or SAML NameIDs.

Target: we'd like the package by EOD Aug 4 to stay on our SIG intake timeline. Let me know if any of those items require additional approvals from your side.

Appreciate it,
Elena Ortiz
InfoSec Lead | AlphaMed

---
Attachment request: list of required artifacts (no files attached yet)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena@alphamed.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG intake — initial list of access artifacts we need

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear checklist. We can deliver the package and will include a short index (README) mapping each file to the SIG/CAIQ questions. High-level plan below: 

1) Canary bundle (anonymized 10-user sample) by Thu 31 Jul EOD PST — includes: SCIM sample, one SAML assertion sample per role, and an exported RBAC slice.
2) Full package (zipped, with index.md) by Tue 4 Aug EOD PST — includes full SCIM delta (30d) + snapshot, RBAC matrix v2, saml_assertions_sample.zip, provisioning runbook excerpts, and session/MFA metrics.
3) Redaction: we will redact user-visible emails in the canary bundle but keep NameIDs and saml timestamps intact; full package will contain a manifest indicating PII locations so your team can choose whether to accept or request additional anonymization.

Attachments in the canary bundle (we'll attach in follow-up email): SIG-access-inventory.csv (index), SCIM-export-20250728.json (sample), RBAC-matrix-v2.xlsx (slice), saml_assertions_sample.zip (2 assertion .xml files).

Rachel will coordinate the SCIM export and Ben will own the RBAC rationale doc. If that's ok I'll proceed and upload the canary bundle to a restricted Drive folder and share a link with your team.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sales & Security Liaison | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Elena Ortiz <elena@alphamed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG intake — initial list of access artifacts we need

Marissa / Elena — quick technical notes on the SCIM export and redaction so expectations match: 

- Export type: we can produce both a full snapshot (CSV/JSON) and a 30-day delta (SCIM change events). The delta is exported as a consumer-friendly JSON array; filename will be SCIM-export-20250728.json for the sample.
- Service accounts: by default our SCIM export includes service account objects; we can tag them with "service:true" in the sample and exclude sensitive secret fields. Please confirm whether you want service accounts omitted entirely from the canary or just flagged.
- Provisioning timestamps: the export contains created/updated timestamps and a provisioning_owner attribute (email) which helps map tickets back to owners. We'll include a CSV mapping of ticket IDs for recent deprovisions.
- SAML: the assertion samples are real assertions captured from an internal test tenant — they will include NameID and Issuer values; we will not include raw user passwords or private keys. 

Drive path (will be restricted): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleLink — I'll upload the canary package there and share the folder to the two external addresses.

Please confirm: 1) remove service accounts from the canary or 2) keep flagged service accounts in sample? Also confirm whether we should redact all email addresses (we recommend leaving NameIDs for assertion integrity).

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Sr. Product Security Engineer | Redwood Inference

Full RBAC export will include role-to-user mappings in the complete package behind the manifest.

2) Please include a tiny README that explains any transformations you applied (PII redaction, omitted attributes).
